algorithm: dual-network "System 1, System 2" VLA: S2 (7B VLM, 7-9Hz) produces a continuous latent conditioning vector consumed by S1 (80M-param cross-attention encoder-decoder transformer, 200Hz); trained end-to-end with a "standard regression loss" (no diffusion/flow-matching, no formula given)
arm: Figure humanoid, full upper body (wrists, torso, head, fingers); demonstrated on one and on two Figure robots simultaneously with identical weights
note_gaps: No success rate, trial count, or comparison table anywhere on the page for any task; the hand itself is never named, given a model number, or assigned a DoF count separate from the whole-body 35-DoF figure; "thousands of novel items" describes the attempted object pool, not a train/test split or a success count.
action_head: 80M-parameter cross-attention encoder-decoder transformer (System 1), continuous 35-DoF whole-upper-body output at 200Hz (wrist poses, finger flexion/abduction, torso, head orientation, plus a synthetic task-completion action), no action tokenization
pretrain_data: ~500 hours of multi-robot, multi-operator teleoperated data, hindsight-labeled with natural-language instructions by an auto-labeling VLM
dexterous_evidence: The page claims individual-finger control is part of the 35-DoF whole-upper-body action space ("Helix coordinates a 35-DoF action space at 200Hz, controlling everything from individual finger movements to end-effector trajectories...", Results) and shows it in multiple demo videos on real Figure robots, but reports no success rate, no trial count, and no table for any task on any hand — the only quantitative evaluation claim is a data-efficiency comparison ("<5%" the data of unnamed prior VLA datasets), not a task outcome.
